design_detail: Secondary pooled analysis of placebo-controlled, double-blind laboratory studies of oral MDMA run separately at three sites: San Francisco (45 people), Chicago (95) and Basel (80), 220 healthy volunteers in all. Volunteers received placebo or MDMA (1.5 mg/kg at San Francisco and Chicago; a fixed 125 mg at Basel); the models carry participant as a random effect, which implies placebo and MDMA sessions in the same person, but the paper does not say so outright and gives no number of sessions per person, order or spacing. Some of the original studies had further sessions (other doses, an active comparison drug, a pretreatment medicine) that are not analysed. Peak change from baseline in heart rate, blood pressure and five 100-mm visual analogue ratings was compared across sites with multilevel linear models (fixed effects drug, site and sex; random effects past MDMA use and participant). A second analysis related each person's lifetime number of earlier MDMA uses (log of 1 plus the number) to the peak rating or reading after MDMA, site by site. Some San Francisco and Chicago data were unpublished at the time.
can_establish: Whether, in 220 healthy volunteers tested at three sites, a single oral dose of MDMA raised heart rate, blood pressure and ratings of drug effect, drug liking and stimulation to a similar degree at sites that differed in participants' MDMA experience, instructions, whether staff were in the room and whether people lay in bed; that ratings of closeness to others and of anxiety after MDMA differed between some sites; and, as an association between different people, that a higher number of earlier MDMA uses went with a lower 'any drug effect' rating at the two sites that tested experienced people (significant in Chicago, a trend in San Francisco).
cannot_establish: That the sites are equivalent (no equivalence test; a non-significant site difference in groups of 45 to 95 does not show the effects are the same); the size of any effect (the text prints no means, SDs or effect sizes for MDMA against placebo; they are in Figure 2, an image not extracted); anything about doses other than about 1.5 mg/kg (Basel's fixed 125 mg averaged 1.89 mg/kg, 26% more per kilogram than 1.5 mg/kg; editors' calculation); that earlier use made the response weaker (the use-history analysis compares different people; age, other drugs, why people kept using and recall of past use are not controlled; the decline is significant at one site only, Chicago, with San Francisco at trend level, and Basel shows a significant rise in the opposite direction); the response of people new to MDMA outside Basel (the other two sites required earlier use); sex differences (the paper says sex changed no result and prints no statistics); events outside the laboratory such as heat, dancing, crowding, other drugs or pills of unknown content.

sample.recruitment: Not described beyond healthy young adults screened for psychiatric and medical problems at all three sites; the source of volunteers and any payment are not stated in this paper (Methods and Materials > Participants, 1st paragraph).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Similar across sites with differences in current drug use: current alcohol and nicotine use allowed at all sites (smoking limited to fewer than 7 cigarettes a day in Basel and fewer than 10 in Chicago); current cannabis use excluded in Basel only; some earlier MDMA use required in Chicago and San Francisco but not in Basel; a negative test for alcohol and other drugs before each session at every site. Excluded: a current Axis I disorder including substance dependence (DSM-IV) and any cardiovascular or neurological disorder that would raise risk (Methods and Materials > Participants, 1st paragraph).
sample.demographics: Age 25.4 (SD 5.2) years and weight 68.8 (SD 11.6) kg overall; 44% women; lifetime MDMA use from 0 to 200 occasions. By site (Table 1): age 28.0 (6.7), 24.3 (4.5) and 25.4 (5.2); lifetime uses 32.8 (37.0), 13.1 (13.5) and 0.6 (0.6) for San Francisco, Chicago and Basel. 35 people, all in Basel, had never taken MDMA outside the laboratory. Other drug histories were not available for San Francisco; in Basel 79 of 80 drank alcohol and 69 had used cannabis at least once; in Chicago 89 of 95 drank alcohol and 75 currently smoked cannabis (about 10 days a month) (Results > Participants).
sample.attrition: The paper counts the 220 who completed the study procedures; how many were enrolled and how many dropped out are not reported.
sample.selection_effects: Volunteers screened to be healthy. At San Francisco and Chicago they were chosen because they had used MDMA before; at Basel most were new to it, so site and experience are mixed up. Chicago volunteers were told they might receive a stimulant, sedative, cannabinoid or placebo (the Discussion also lists an opioid; Table 1 does not) and were alone; San Francisco and Basel volunteers were told MDMA or placebo and had researchers in the room. People who completed the study are the only ones described.

exposure.measurement: Oral capsules given double blind: placebo or MDMA by weight (1.5 mg/kg at San Francisco and Chicago) or a fixed 125 mg (Basel). Abstinence from drugs and alcohol checked by urine (all sites) and breath (San Francisco, Chicago) before each session; pregnancy test for women. The paper does not say where the MDMA came from or whether its content was checked.
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions only: one oral dose per session, 1.5 mg/kg (San Francisco, Chicago) or 125 mg (Basel; Table 1 gives 1.89 mg/kg, SD 0.33), given in the morning (Table 1: 11 am San Francisco, 9:30 am Chicago, 8 to 9 am Basel). Lifetime earlier MDMA use 0 to 200 occasions, by self-report.
exposure.polysubstance: Volunteers tested negative for alcohol and other drugs before each session; current alcohol and nicotine use allowed everywhere, current cannabis use in Chicago and San Francisco but not Basel; no data on other drugs for San Francisco. Other drug use is not an adjustment variable in the models.
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: Urine tests at all sites and breath tests at San Francisco and Chicago before each session; no minimum time since the last MDMA use is stated.

comparison.controls: Placebo in the same people (participant as a random effect); some sites' studies also had other conditions. Sites are compared with each other: different people.
comparison.matching: No matching between sites. Sites differ in age, MDMA experience, nationality, language, dose per kilogram, time of day, instructions about possible drugs, whether researchers were present and whether people lay in bed or walked about.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Why people had used MDMA, the amounts and the content of pills in earlier use, other drug use outside Basel and Chicago, and personality are not measured; the use-history analysis has no measurement from before the first use.
comparison.controls_other_drug_use: Not applicable (no separate control group); people who currently used cannabis were included in Chicago and San Francisco and excluded in Basel.

outcomes.instruments: Heart rate and blood pressure; five visual analogue scales on a 100-mm line from not at all to extremely: any drug effect, liking the drug effects, stimulated, anxious, closeness to others; measured at baseline and repeatedly for several hours; analysed as peak change from baseline (Methods and Materials > Procedure, Dependent Measures, and Drug; Data Analysis).
outcomes.validity_norms: Single-item visual analogue scales; no validation or norms given; the cardiovascular devices are not described.
outcomes.operationalization: One peak value per person and condition. Earlier MDMA use was transformed to the log of 1 plus the number of occasions (base not stated) to reduce non-normal residuals.
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None stated; p < 0.05 for all analyses. Editors' count of 8: heart rate, systolic and diastolic pressure and the five visual analogue ratings; the text says some data are not shown.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Double blind by design; no check of whether volunteers could tell MDMA from placebo; they were told different things about the possible drugs (MDMA or placebo at San Francisco and Basel; stimulant, sedative, cannabinoid or placebo in Chicago).

analysis.effect_sizes: The text prints no means, SDs, effect sizes or test statistics for MDMA against placebo or for the site comparisons, only p-value ranges: cardiovascular site comparisons p = 0.15 to 1.00; peak ratings of any drug effect, drug liking and stimulation after MDMA p = 0.07 to 1.00; values are in Figures 1 and 2 (images, not extracted). Printed for use history: use-by-site interaction for any drug effect F(2, 218) = 4.74, p = 0.010; the rating fell by 6.8 points (95% CI 0.913 to 12.7) for each unit of log(1 + earlier uses) in Chicago, by 5.8 (CI -1.00 to 12.53; p = 0.094) in San Francisco and by 6.1 (CI 2.18 to 10.0) in the two together; in Basel it rose by 13.5 points (CI 1.63 to 25.3). No other relation between past use and an acute effect was significant.
analysis.covariates: Drug, site and sex as fixed effects; past MDMA use and participant as random effects; the authors state sex altered no result (no statistics). Age, other drug use and dose per kilogram are not adjusted for.
analysis.preregistration_detail: The paper reports no registration of this pooled analysis and cites none for the source studies. It says some of the data were published before (Harris et al. 2002; Bedi et al. 2010; Hysek et al. 2012) and some, from San Francisco and Chicago, were not; by authorship the three papers belong to the San Francisco, Chicago and Basel groups.
analysis.selective_reporting: The abstract and Conclusion present the sites' agreement as established, but the drug-against-placebo statistics are not printed; subjective results are given as p-value ranges and by figure, and the text says some data are not shown. Only one of five ratings was related to earlier use. The abstract says the inverse relation held at the sites that tested more experienced people; in San Francisco alone it was at trend level (p = 0.094).
analysis.power: No power calculation; the authors treat 220 individual-level records as a strength. Sites of 45 to 95 people can miss moderate differences, and the slope intervals are wide (0.9 to 12.7 points in Chicago).

interpretation_gap.results_show: In 220 healthy volunteers at three sites a single oral dose of MDMA raised heart rate, blood pressure and subjective ratings. The text reports no significant site difference in peak ratings of any drug effect, drug liking or stimulation after MDMA (p = 0.07 to 1.00), higher peak anxious ratings in Chicago, where people were tested alone, than at the other two sites, and higher closeness to others in San Francisco than in Basel; after placebo, Chicago volunteers rated drug effect and liking higher than the others. A higher number of earlier MDMA uses went with a lower any-drug-effect rating in Chicago (significant) and San Francisco (trend) and a higher one in Basel (fewer than three earlier uses). No size of any effect is printed in the text.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract and Conclusion say MDMA's effects are robust and reproducible across settings, that cardiovascular and subjective effects were very similar at the sites, and that there is modest evidence of tolerance in people who use it regularly; the Discussion calls the data the strongest support so far for repeated use weakening the subjective experience and says they give little support for a much stronger first response.

timeline.event: Harris et al., subjective and hormonal effects of MDMA (cited here as earlier publication of some data; by authorship the San Francisco group).
Bedi et al., prosocial feelings and identification of emotions (cited here as earlier publication of some data; by authorship the Chicago group).
Hysek and Liechti, pupillary light reflex after MDMA alone and after pretreatments (cited here as earlier publication of some data; by authorship the Basel group).
Pooled analysis of nine Basel studies in 166 volunteers; it probably overlaps this paper's Basel group of 80 (five studies of 16 fit that number) but neither paper says so.

replication.where_it_stands: A rise in heart rate, blood pressure and positive ratings after one oral dose in laboratory settings is reported by several independent laboratories, and this paper is itself the cross-laboratory comparison; its statement of similarity is not quantified in the text. The link between earlier use and a weaker any-drug-effect rating rests on this paper alone and on one of five ratings.

funding.funder: Grants DA02812 and DA026570 (Chicago, H. de Wit principal investigator), DA017716 and DA016776 (San Francisco, J. E. Mendelson) and SNSF320030_138481 and SNFF32323B_144996 (Basel, M. E. Liechti), as printed (Acknowledgements); the paper does not spell out the funders' names (editors' reading of the prefixes: the US National Institute on Drug Abuse and the Swiss National Science Foundation).
funding.affiliations_note: The authors include the principal investigators of the three sites whose data are pooled, so the paper reports on the groups' own studies; the Basel data probably also feed Vizeli and Liechti (2017).

what_would_settle_it: A prospective study that gives the same measured dose, with the same instructions and setting, to volunteers who are new to MDMA and to volunteers with a range of earlier use, at more than one site, with pre-specified equivalence margins for the subjective ratings and earlier use recorded in detail (number, amounts, last use, content of pills); and a within-person repeat of the laboratory session in people who go on to use MDMA outside the laboratory.

domains.note: Double blind is stated; whether session order was randomised or counterbalanced, and the gap between sessions, are not given in this paper, and some of the original studies had further sessions (other doses, an active drug, a pretreatment).
Washout intervals are not reported here, so carryover cannot be judged.

Volunteers were told different things about the possible drugs; placebo ratings of drug effect and liking differed by site, which the authors link to expectancy; whether people could tell MDMA from placebo was not checked.
Only the 220 who completed the procedures are described; enrolment and dropout are not reported.
Single-item self-ratings by people who may have known the condition; devices not described; sites differed in time of day and setting (in bed or ambulatory; researchers present or absent).
No registration; p-value ranges printed in place of effect sizes; some results not shown; only one of five ratings related to earlier use; no correction for multiple tests.

domains.domain: Use-history and between-site analyses (added by the editors; not a RoB 2 domain)
domains.note: Correlational and between different people: age, other drug use, recall of past use and site are mixed up (the sites differ in age and in how much earlier use they allowed); the sign is opposite in Basel; the log base is not stated.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: The comparison of MDMA with placebo in the same people is at some concerns at worst, but its numbers are not printed in the text, so the source cannot give the size of effects. The overall judgment is set by the cross-site and use-history analyses, which are observational. The source may be cited for the design and sample; for the statement that three sites reported similar peak ratings of drug effect, drug liking and stimulation, with named differences in closeness to others and anxiety; and for the observation that the any-drug-effect rating was lower with more earlier use at two sites. It should not be cited for the size of effects, for equivalence between sites, for tolerance as a cause, or for sex differences.

key_findings.finding: Three sites pooled: San Francisco 45 people (20 women, 25 men; 1.5 mg/kg; researchers present; 11 am), Chicago 95 (37 women, 58 men; 1.5 mg/kg; people alone; 9:30 am; told they might receive a stimulant, sedative, cannabinoid or placebo) and Basel 80 (40 women, 40 men; a fixed 125 mg, 1.89 mg/kg (SD 0.33); researchers present; 8 to 9 am; told MDMA or placebo).

220 volunteers (44% women), age 25.4 (SD 5.2), weight 68.8 (SD 11.6) kg; lifetime MDMA use 0 to 200 occasions, 32.8 (SD 37.0) in San Francisco, 13.1 (13.5) in Chicago and 0.6 (0.6) in Basel; 35 people, all in Basel, had never taken MDMA outside the laboratory. San Francisco volunteers were older and more experienced than the other two groups, and Chicago more experienced than Basel (all p < 0.05).

MDMA raised heart rate and blood pressure to a similar degree at the three sites (site comparison p = 0.15 to 1.00) and produced similar reports on most subjective ratings; peak ratings of any drug effect, drug liking and stimulation after MDMA did not differ between sites (p = 0.07 to 1.00). The values are in Figures 1 and 2, which are images and were not extracted.
key_findings.locator: Results > Acute Effects of MDMA across Sites, 1st paragraph; Figures 1 and 2
key_findings.note: No means or effect sizes in the text; absence of a significant site difference is not equivalence.

key_findings.finding: Site differences: after MDMA, Chicago volunteers gave higher peak anxious ratings than San Francisco and Basel volunteers, and San Francisco volunteers higher peak closeness to others than Basel volunteers (p < 0.05 for each); after placebo, Chicago volunteers gave higher peak drug effect and drug liking than the other two sites (p < 0.01) and Basel volunteers had lower peak systolic and diastolic pressure (p < 0.05).
key_findings.locator: Results > Acute Effects of MDMA across Sites, 1st paragraph

key_findings.finding: Earlier use: the any-drug-effect rating after MDMA related to lifetime MDMA use differently by site (use-by-site F(2, 218) = 4.74, p = 0.010). It fell by 6.8 points (95% CI 0.913 to 12.7) per unit of log(1 + earlier uses) in Chicago, by 5.8 (CI -1.00 to 12.53; p = 0.094) in San Francisco and by 6.1 (CI 2.18 to 10.0) in the two together; in Basel, where people had used MDMA fewer than three times or not at all, it rose by 13.5 (CI 1.63 to 25.3). No other relation between earlier use and an acute effect reached significance.
key_findings.locator: Results > Relationship between acute drug-related effects and MDMA use history, 1st paragraph; Figure 3
key_findings.note: The log base is not stated, so slopes cannot be converted to points per additional use.

key_findings.finding: The authors read the finding as modest evidence of tolerance in people with heavier use and as little support for the idea that the first experience is much stronger than later ones. They offer other explanations: people with heavier use may also use other potent drugs, tolerance may be specific to the setting, and the any-drug-effect rating is a global item that may be more sensitive than the others.

The authors suggest, without testing it, that having researchers in the room (San Francisco, Basel) may have raised prosocial and lowered negative ratings compared with being alone (Chicago), and note that closeness ratings fell with earlier use in San Francisco at trend level (p = 0.07).

Sex: the paper states that participant sex did not alter any result and discusses it no further in the Results; the Discussion notes that other studies found women reported stronger subjective responses.
key_findings.locator: Data Analysis, last sentence; Discussion, 7th paragraph

reporting_issues.issue: The text prints no means, SDs or test statistics for the effect of MDMA against placebo on any rating or on heart rate and blood pressure, and gives site comparisons only as p-value ranges; the values are in figures.
reporting_issues.consequence: The size of the effects, and how close the sites are, cannot be read from the text; the claim of very similar effects rests on non-significance in groups of 45 to 95.

reporting_issues.issue: The Introduction says all sites gave comparable, moderate doses (1.5 mg/kg or 125 mg), but Table 1 gives 1.89 mg/kg (SD 0.33) at Basel against 1.5 at the other sites, 26% more per kilogram (editors' calculation).
reporting_issues.consequence: Basel's dose per kilogram was higher; agreement across sites despite this is informative, but the doses are not the same.

reporting_issues.issue: The use-by-site interaction is printed with 2 and 218 degrees of freedom. A model with site, earlier use and their interaction fitted to 220 people has 214 residual degrees of freedom (editors' calculation); 218 would fit a model with one predictor. The printed p (0.010) is the same either way.
reporting_issues.consequence: No effect on the result; the model is not fully described.

reporting_issues.issue: Earlier use was transformed as the log of 1 plus the number of occasions without saying which base.
reporting_issues.consequence: Slopes of 5.8 to 13.5 points per unit cannot be turned into points per extra use; with base 10 or base e they differ by a factor of about 2.3.

reporting_issues.issue: The abstract says the inverse relation between earlier use and the any-drug-effect rating held at the sites testing more experienced people; Chicago alone was significant (p < 0.05) and San Francisco alone was at trend level (p = 0.094); the two together were significant.
reporting_issues.consequence: Evidence of a lower rating with more use rests mainly on Chicago and on pooling two sites; it is one of five ratings tested.

verification.source_read: PMC full text PMC4161650 (author manuscript), read in the app's browser: abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Table 1, figure legends, funding and conflict statements. Figures 1 to 3 are images and were not read for values. No supplementary files exist or were read.
